statusDetail: All 58 catalog checks have conclusive outcomes across four representative archetypes plus a failure-state route.

page.notes: Vietnamese lottery results/content site. Coverage includes results, analysis, interactive trial and news listing. Date-specific archive pages and every province/template variant were not repeated because they share the same global shell and result-table archetype; no purchase/account flow exists.

principleOutcomes.reason: This public lottery results/content site exposes no declared agent-facing transaction or productivity capability; emerging WebMCP support is therefore contextual and not required. paths.description: Homepage and current southern lottery results, the primary results-reading journey and shared global template.
Southern analysis page, representing editorial/prediction detail pages.
Lottery trial tool, representing the site’s primary interactive/tool archetype.
News listing, representing content index/navigation pages.
Representative invalid URL to inspect HTTP failure handling.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is byte-identical to the light capture; colorScheme is normal and body text remains rgb(51,51,51).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define dark surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the primary content on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and all three representative mobile paths open with a viewport-dominating modal over results/content; the mobile dialog occupies nearly the full screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-first consent surface where legally permissible, preserve equally prominent accept/reject choices, and avoid covering the primary task.

findings.summary: Route and state changes have no View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The preferences/CSS probe found no view-transition usage on a multi-page site with many route changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same- and cross-document navigation with View Transitions while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware navigation chrome.
findings.evidence: After scrolling 800px the static header and nav move fully off-screen; no scroll timeline or scroll-state CSS was detected on a 14,363px page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained sticky or shrinking header, or a progress/return affordance, using CSS scroll-state features with a simple fallback.

findings.summary: Components adapt only at the page level, with no container-query behavior detected.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules despite dense tables/cards reused across a responsive layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container-type and @container for reusable result/table modules that appear at different inline sizes.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly styled and most targets are below the recommended touch size.
findings.evidence: Focused controls reported outline-style none and no box shadow; 243 of 246 rendered focusables measured below 44px in at least one dimension, including the 36x28 menu button.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible indicator and increase compact navigation/control hit areas to about 44x44 CSS pixels without forcing visual bulk.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 8.46s (performance 0.71); the trace corroborated one 107.65ms long task and 57.65ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP content, delay consent/ad work that is not required for first render, and verify LCP under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking scripts and font delivery delay main content.
findings.evidence: HAR+DOM confirmation found synchronous parser-inserted jQuery, jQuery UI, and two site bundles; Lighthouse estimated 850ms render-blocking savings and flagged font display/cache issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, remove the critical-path dependency on jQuery UI where possible, subset/self-host only needed fonts, and set useful cache headers.

findings.summary: The page ships a large amount of unused JavaScript, dominated by third parties.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 455KiB unused JavaScript; HAR recorded 721,728 transferred script bytes, including 190KB ads and 167KB tag-manager scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Load advertising/analytics only after the relevant consent and need, remove duplicate legacy libraries, and split first-party bundles by route.

findings.summary: Dense result tables and some controls lack robust accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed table caption/header relationships; DOM found 17 links without text/aria-label/img alt, and result radio controls have empty labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Add real captions and scoped headers to data tables, label radio controls, and provide accessible names for every link/control.

findings.summary: Some foreground/background color combinations fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility audit failed color-contrast even though the aggregate accessibility score was 0.97.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the failing text/control tokens to meet at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text and essential UI.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and heading structure are disrupted by the consent implementation.
findings.evidence: Focus probes found no visible outline; the accessibility tree-facing DOM contains four extra H1s from consent UI in addition to the page H1.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore visible focus styles and ensure embedded consent UI does not pollute the document heading hierarchy.

findings.summary: Touch-target sizing is inadequate across the dense navigation and result controls.
findings.evidence: 243 of 246 visible focusables measured under 44px in width or height; while reflow had only 1px overflow, target size remains a broad mobile usability barrier.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas using padding/pseudo-elements while preserving the compact table layout, then retest at 200% zoom and 360px width.

findings.summary: Several images lack intrinsic dimensions or responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 2 images without dimensions, one 710px logo displayed at 200px, 3 missing srcset, and 3 legacy-format images; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width/height or aspect-ratio, provide responsive srcset/sizes, and encode appropriate assets in WebP/AVIF where beneficial.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy were absent; all 3 observed analytics/consent cookies lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, a nonce/hash-based CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark cookies Secure and use the least-permissive SameSite value.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising dominate the network before a consent choice.
findings.evidence: The fresh load contacted 11 third-party origins and 6 known tracker domains; 25 third-party requests transferred 758,644 bytes, about 89% of the 853,445-byte load.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to no non-essential tracking before consent, minimize vendors, and batch only the analytics events needed for a stated purpose.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no HSTS, clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy, and no CSP from which frame-ancestors or Trusted Types could be enforced.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy the missing browser policies in report-only mode first, then enforce a tested CSP and framing policy.

findings.summary: The installable-looking site has a manifest but no service worker or offline fallback.
findings.evidence: manifest.json declares standalone display/start_url, but the capabilities probe found zero service-worker registrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a minimal service worker and useful offline fallback for previously viewed results/static guidance, with explicit stale-data messaging.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not fully optimized for its display sizes.
findings.evidence: Images evidence found an oversized 710px logo rendered at 200px, no modern-format images, missing responsive sources, and missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve appropriately sized responsive images and modern formats, preserving intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume a disproportionate resource budget for a text-and-table results site.
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 758,644 of 853,445 bytes; ad/tag/consent scripts are the five largest network resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party byte/request budget, defer vendors until needed and consented, and remove vendors that do not support the core result-reading task.
